about.title: About Me
paragraphs: I'm a Ph.D. student in Mechanical Engineering at Villanova University, working in the Laboratory for Advanced Thermal and Fluid Systems. My research focuses on Flow Network Modeling, thermal-fluid system analysis, experimental validation, and Digital Twin development for large-scale, high-power data center cooling systems.
My current work spans two-phase cooling component modeling in Flownex, system-level integration of vendor hardware and experimental data, and interactive Digital Twin development in NVIDIA Omniverse.

items.title: OMNICOOL — 1 MW-Class Two-Phase Data Center Cooling System (ARPA-E)
items.text: Developing system-level thermal-hydraulic models for a 1 MW-class two-phase direct-to-chip data center cooling system, with current work focused on a 250 kW unit. Integrating vendor hardware information, equipment performance data, experimental measurements, and system requirements into physics-based Flow Network Models.

items.title: ES2 Project 5.1 — Single-Phase vs. Two-Phase Data Center Cooling
items.text: Performed comparative thermal-fluid simulations of single-phase and two-phase data center cooling architectures to evaluate thermal response, cooling performance, flow behavior, and system-level operating characteristics under varying heat loads.

items.title: Two-Phase Data Center Component Library — Flownex
items.text: Developed a dedicated two-phase data center cooling component library in the Flownex Simulation Environment, including cold plates, quick disconnects, flow regulators, and heat exchangers. Developed and validated component models using experimental data and established two-phase heat-transfer and pressure-drop correlations.

items.title: Thermal-Fluid Experimental Test Bench
items.text: Designed and constructed a thermal-fluid experimental bench for testing and characterization of cold-plate geometries, including skived-fin, porous-foam, and gyroid structures. Performed flow-loop assembly, sensor installation and wiring, instrumentation, measurement-system setup, and data acquisition.

items.title: Digital Twin — NVIDIA Omniverse
items.text: Developed a physics-based Digital Twin architecture coupling thermal-fluid system simulation with telemetry, parametric controls, and 3D visualization for monitoring and analysis of data center cooling systems.
